- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 3–5 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for sudden upward moves.
- Model overestimates downward moves in the 10+ day horizon; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for extended bearish sentiment.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 2–3σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–20% for next 3–5 days; if below, increase by 10–20%.
- Overshoot after spikes: if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5%, reduce next forecast by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., bullish → bearish) triggers 1–2 day lag correction: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude by 50%.
